What life there is like day to day
How it compares with where you live now

start a stable life in one place

model: If I could live anywhere, I'd choose Melbourne in Australia. I've never actually been there, but my cousin moved there to study about five years ago, and she's told me so much about it that I feel I almost know the place. From what she says, it offers a really high quality of life. There are huge green spaces right in the city centre, like the Royal Botanic Gardens, and there's an old tram network that makes public transport easy. Her flat is in a suburb which is only fifteen minutes from the city, and there's a market, a library and a beach all within walking distance. Another thing that appeals to me is that it's a real melting pot. There are large Vietnamese, Greek and Italian communities, so the food scene is supposed to be one of the best in the world, and I wouldn't feel too homesick. Compared with Ho Chi Minh City, the streets are quieter and cleaner, and people seem to have a better work-life balance. My cousin finishes work at five and goes running by the river, which almost never happens here. Of course, the cost of living is much higher, and I've heard the weather is unpredictable, sometimes with four seasons in one day. But for me those are small problems. It's the kind of city where I could imagine settling down in the future.
